articles.title_orig: Resetting expectations for these six NFL teams with injured quarterbacks: Giants eyeing draft again
articles.title_zh: 重新设定对这六支四分卫受伤的NFL球队的期望：巨人队再次关注选秀
articles.summary_zh: 到目前为止，四分卫受伤一直是2026年NFL赛季的不幸故事。在第二周的训练营中，六名先发球员的缺席使联盟近四分之一的场上比赛黯然失色。幸运的是，许多伤病都是短期问题，只有轻微的破坏竞选的风险，但在少数情况下，几乎没有理由乐观。
articles.content_orig:
Quarterback injuries have been the unfortunate story of the 2026 NFL season thus far. The loss of six starters from training camp through Week 2 overshadows on-field play for nearly one quarter of the league. Fortunately, many of the injuries are short-term issues with only a slight risk of derailing the campaign, but in a couple of cases, there is little reason for optimism.
The New York Giants might be in the worst position of any of the six teams that lost their starters. Jaxson Dart sustained a knee injury on "Monday Night Football" that, upon further testing, is more severe than the team initially feared. If any of the NFL's injured signal-callers are to miss the rest of the year, Dart is the most likely candidate.
If it is indeed a season-ender for Dart, the Giants' 2026 goals shift dramatically. For other teams, like the Seattle Seahawks , expectations remain largely unchanged even in the face of injury.
Here are reasonable expectations for all six teams with injured quarterbacks.
Injured player: Jaxson Dart (knee)
New expectations: Vie for another early draft pick
There is no sugar coating the Giants' outlook without Dart. What had all the makings of a (finally) exciting year is already down the tubes. The offense looked hapless with Jameis Winston on in relief against the Los Angeles Rams , and while the veteran has had decent stretches in the past, his diminished arm strength, persistent turnover problems and the immense downgrade in mobility he brings compared to Dart puts a firm ceiling on the Giants.
Winston will potentially man the offense for the remainder of the year after Dart's MRI revealed a worse injury than expected. In five games without Dart since his arrival as a first-round pick, the Giants are 0-5. That history suggests that so long as Winston is the man under center, New York will stand among the worst teams in the NFL. The silver lining is that the Giants should be able to add more premium young talent to their enticing core in the 2027 draft, but this was supposed to be a season in which that group elevated them out of the early draft pick range and into playoff contention.
Injured players: Caleb Williams (hamstring), Tyson Bagent (concussion)
New expectations: Fall into early-season hole, climb out when Williams returns
The hamstring issue that knocked Williams out of the Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings initially looked like it would result in a long-term absence. Instead, the rising star is week-to-week and could even return as soon as Monday's battle with the Philadelphia Eagles . It would be aggressive to bring him back from a soft-tissue injury in such short order, though, and with Bagent suffering a concussion , there is a real chance the Bears roll out their No. 3 quarterback on "Monday Night Football." Case Keenum might make his first appearance since 2023.
If it ends up being no more than a one-game absence for Williams, the Bears will likely be 1-2 upon his return. The early-season losses might hold Chicago back from reaching its loftiest regular-season goals, but by no means would they dash the Bears' hopes of reaching the playoffs. The offense is electric enough with Williams in the lineup to rattle off a bunch of victories. Remember, this team started 0-2 a year ago and reached the divisional round of the playoffs.
Injured player: Jayden Daniels (dislocated elbow)
New expectations: Another losing season incoming
With two losses already on their ledger, the Commanders are in extreme danger of falling back into the NFL's bottom tier for a second consecutive season. It is difficult to foresee them stringing together wins with Daniels on the sideline, particularly because their next six games include matchups against the NFC West's top three teams and a rematch with the Eagles squad that defeated them in Week 1. Washington might have to attack that entire stretch with Marcus Mariota under center.
The dislocated elbow is the exact same injury Daniels sustained in Week 9 last year. He missed four weeks and reinjured the elbow in his return and sat out the remainder of the season. The recurring nature of this issue sounds alarms about Daniels' ability to stay on the field this year and beyond. And the rest of the team is not strong enough to stay afloat without him. The defense, for instance, ranks 27th in scoring through two games.
Injured player: Sam Darnold (glute)
New expectations: Contend for second consecutive Super Bowl
Drew Lock did just enough to lead the Seahawks to a season-opening win when thrust into action in the first quarter, and following a full week of preparation for the road opener at the Arizona Cardinals , he excelled with three touchdowns in a 31-7 win. Seattle should be in business for as long as it needs to roll out its backup.
Even better news for the Seahawks is that Sam Darnold might return to action this week. Coach Mike Macdonald said he anticipates Darnold suiting up for practice, and the extent of his participation will determine his availability for Sunday's matchup against the Commanders. Assuming the offense is back at full strength no later than Week 4, the Seahawks have a good chance of remaining undefeated in time for Darnold's return. They cannot ask for much more than that.
Injured player: Kyler Murray (concussion)
New expectations: Battle for NFC North title
The concussion Murray suffered in the first quarter of the season opener looked grim, but it will result in only a one-game absence. Murray cleared concussion protocol and will start in Week 3 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , coach Kevin O'Connell announced. Thanks to Carson Wentz and two solid performances, Murray inherits a 2-0 record for his return.
In a division where every other team is 1-1 and where the Bears have quarterback injuries, the Packers look flawed, and the Lions ' defense is a mess, Minnesota has a chance to build a comfortable early-season cushion. None of the teams on their schedule until Week 9 made the playoffs in 2025. If Murray delivers the career resurgence the Vikings hoped he would when they signed him in free agency, he could lead them to a terrific first half of the season.
Injured player: Michael Penix Jr . (torn ACL), Tua Tagovailoa (oblique)
New expectations: Prevent disastrous season after 0-2 start
The Cooper Rush experience was dismal. Back-to-back losses and a 34-3 drubbing at the hands of a division rival made the Falcons look like one of the NFL's worst teams through two weeks. Help is on the way, though. Penix is cleared for action and will take over as the starter in Week 3 , and Tagovailoa returned to full participation in practice, setting him up to assume backup duties. Health willing, Atlanta will not need to turn back to its No. 3 quarterback.
The problem is that Penix is not guaranteed to be an upgrade. He is 4-8 as a starter since his arrival in 2024 and has an immense injury history. He ought to be able to make better use of his elite offensive supporting cast than Rush, but it would require a breakout season from the third-year pro in order for the Falcons to erase their 0-2 start and finish the year above .500. And if things go sideways for Penix or he returns to the injury report, Tagovailoa carries the exact same shortcomings.
articles.content_zh:
到目前为止，四分卫受伤一直是2026年NFL赛季的不幸故事。在第二周的训练营中，六名先发球员的缺席使联盟近四分之一的场上比赛黯然失色。幸运的是，许多伤病都是短期问题，只有轻微的破坏竞选的风险，但在少数情况下，几乎没有理由乐观。
纽约巨人队可能是六支失去首发球员的球队中最糟糕的一支。Jaxson Dart在“周一晚上足球”中膝盖受伤，经过进一步测试，伤势比球队最初担心的更严重。如果NFL的任何受伤的信号呼叫者错过了今年剩下的时间，Dart是最有可能的候选人。
如果这确实是达特的赛季结束，那么巨人队2026年的进球将发生巨大变化。对于其他球队，如西雅图海鹰队，即使面对伤病，人们的期望也基本保持不变。
以下是对所有六支四分卫受伤的球队的合理预期。
受伤球员：Jaxson Dart（膝盖）
新的期望：期待另一个早期选秀权
没有达特，巨人队的前景就没有糖衣了。（终于）激动人心的一年的所有要素都已经尘埃落定。在面对洛杉矶公羊队的比赛中，Jameis Winston替补上场，进攻看起来很倒霉，虽然这位老将过去有过不错的伸展，但他手臂力量的减弱、持续的失误问题以及与Dart相比他带来的机动性的大幅下降给巨人队带来了严峻的挑战。
在达特的核磁共振成像显示伤势比预期更严重后，温斯顿可能会在今年剩下的时间里担任进攻球员。自从达特作为首轮选秀权加盟以来，在没有达特的五场比赛中，巨人队以0比5获胜。这段历史表明，只要温斯顿是中锋，纽约将成为美国国家橄榄球联盟中最糟糕的球队之一。一线希望是，巨人队应该能够在2027年的选秀中为他们诱人的核心增加更多优秀的年轻人才，但这应该是一个该小组将他们从早期选秀范围提升到季后赛争夺的赛季。
受伤球员：Caleb Williams（腿筋），Tyson Bagent（脑震荡）
新的期望：陷入赛季初的洞，当威廉姆斯回归时爬出来
在第二周输给明尼苏达维京人队的比赛中，威廉姆斯被腿筋问题淘汰出局，最初看起来这将导致他长期缺席。相反，这颗冉冉升起的新星每周都在升起，甚至可能重新升起

articles.title_orig: Kratom found at locations where two Ole Miss students were discovered dead
articles.title_zh: Kratom found at locations where two Ole Miss students were discovered dead
articles.content_orig:
Two University of Mississippi students died this week and packaged kratom was found during the separate death investigations, law enforcement officials said Tuesday.
Authorities said they have not confirmed that kratom or any other substance was a contributing factor in either death.
Lafayette County Metro Narcotics said Tuesday that it has no information that the two deaths are linked.
“However, packaged Kratom sold from a retail store was found during both investigations,” it said in a statement. “Out of an abundance of caution, we encourage everyone to avoid kratom and any other medication or substance that was not prescribed to you or obtained from a trusted, regulated source.”
The Ole Miss students have not been publicly identified by authorities.
Both were found dead Monday; one on campus, and the other in the city of Oxford, Mayor Robyn Tannehill said.
“The University is heartbroken by the recent loss of two students and extends our condolences to their families, friends, and loved ones during this difficult time,” the university said.
The deaths, which are under investigation by local, state and federal authorities, are being treated as separate inquiries, according to Lafayette County Metro Narcotics.
Raegan Settle, a senior who is the student editor-in-chief of the student newspaper “The Daily Mississippian,” said the mood on campus was “really frantic.” A lot of the details were just coming out Tuesday, she said.
“Many students are hanging black ribbons around their sorority and fraternity houses as we speak,” she said. “So, I think people are just really shocked.”
Greek organizations on campus have been reminding members not to take anything that is not prescribed specifically for them by their doctor, Settle said.
Kratom, the name of a product and the Southeast Asia tree from which it comes,  has gained popularity in the U.S. as an unapproved treatment for pain, anxiety and drug dependence. It is sometimes sold at gas stations or online.
Kratom can produce either stimulating or sedating effects, depending on the dosage taken, and can produce psychotic symptoms, according to the Drug Enforcement Administration .
It’s not federally banned, but the DEA lists it as a “drug and chemical of concern.” The Mayo Clinic calls kratom unsafe and ineffective and says it’s been linked to a small number of deaths, but that “nearly all deaths from kratom also involved other drugs or substances.”
Kratom has been banned by local laws in Oxford, Mississippi, but can be bought in surrounding counties, said Capt. Alex Fauver, commander of the Metro Narcotics unit.
“We have a lot of problems with the kratom and people on it, it has no medical use,” he said in a phone interview.
Kratom was found at each student’s residence, he said.
There have been no other student deaths and no other students or members of the community impacted, Fauver and the university said.
Authorities urged people not  to speculate, and acknowledged that there was unverified information being spread online.
Lafayette County Metro Narcotics said there was a “significant amount of concern, speculation, and misinformation circulating.”
Phil Helsel is a reporter for NBC News.
Juliette Arcodia is a producer for NBC News' Southern Region.
George Solis is a national correspondent with NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Austin Police, Travis County DA launch independent investigation into ICE shooting
articles.title_zh: Austin Police, Travis County DA launch independent investigation into ICE shooting
articles.content_orig:
Austin police and the Travis County District Attorney's Office say they are actively investigating the shooting of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez by an ICE officer. But so far, it's not clear how much evidence they'll be able to access from the Department of Homeland Security, which is conducting a separate investigation of the incident.
During a news conference on Tuesday, APD Chief Lisa Davis said her detectives are speaking "daily" with DHS and she had no reason to believe the department would withhold information. She said she didn't know what her detectives had requested or when they expected to receive it.
"These are some of our most elite investigators," she said. "They are fantastic. I trust them. I trust this investigation and it is absolutely in good hands."
She also said APD is investigating the shooting alongside Texas Rangers and the Travis County District Attorney's Office.
District Attorney José Garza told KUT that his prosecutors have asked federal investigators for digital and physical evidence to get a "complete accounting" of the shooting. They've also asked to interview the ICE officer who shot Garces Perez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan national.
"We're still awaiting word on whether or not our request will be granted," he said, adding that the investigation is at a "preliminary moment."
Garza also wrote a letter to the agency asking that Garces Perez remain in the country.  A federal judge ruled Tuesday that he must be present for a court hearing in San Antonio on Sept. 30, but Garza said he will need to stay far longer than that while investigators look into the shooting.
"From our perspective, Mr. Garces Perez is a material witness to the incident that took place in Austin," he said. "The Travis County District Attorney's Office thinks that it is critical that he remain in the United States so that he can participate in the investigation and any proceeding that may follow."
The incident comes after a rash of similar shootings by federal immigration agents across the country. Local officials this week expressed concern about whether federal investigators would share all the evidence with APD and Garza's office, citing cases in Minnesota and Houston where federal investigators withheld evidence and slowed local prosecutions.
KUT reached out to DHS to ask if the agency plans to share information with local law enforcement, but the agency did not respond. The FBI, which is assisting in the federal investigation, directed questions about evidence-sharing to DHS.
Correction: This story has been updated to correct the spelling of Garces Perez's first name.

articles.title_orig: Hayden Panettiere died from an overdose involving fentanyl. She had just gone to rehab, coroner says
articles.title_zh: Hayden Panettiere died from an overdose involving fentanyl. She had just gone to rehab, coroner says
articles.content_orig:
The death of Hayden Panettiere last month is now the subject of a federal investigation into whether the actress obtained illicit and possibly counterfeit drugs from a dealer in Southern California, a source familiar with the investigation told CNN.
But building a criminal case from her accidental overdose death will be an uphill challenge for investigators.
Tens of thousands of people die from drug overdose deaths every year, but only a few hundred per year lead to criminal charges. Some celebrity deaths in recent years, notably those of “Friends” actor Matthew Perry and rapper Mac Miller , have led to charges. Others, like the death of the musician Prince , did not.
“These are just really difficult cases, regardless of if you’re a celebrity or if you’re just John Q. Public,” said Thaddeus Johnson, a former law enforcement official in Tennessee and senior fellow at the Council on Criminal Justice think tank.
The challenge for investigators lies in the gritty details. To make the case, they have to follow the trail of evidence, such as phone records, drugs and witnesses, to identify a dealer or supplier. Investigators also have to prove with toxicology, forensic pathology, and medical analysis that the specific drugs caused the victim’s death.
Why it’s important to prosecute celebrity drug deaths and the message it sends, according to legal experts
“Every case is different,” said CNN senior legal analyst Elie Honig, a former prosecutor. “Sometimes you can make a link. Sometimes you can’t.”
These investigations require significant resources, but overdose deaths are often not prioritized by police in the same way as a fatal shooting. Celebrity deaths may be an exception, though.
“It does seem that police are more attentive to and more invested in cases that get a lot of attention when it’s a well-known person who overdoses,” Honig said.
The challenges of bringing these cases are newly relevant as investigators dig into Panettiere’s death .
Panettiere, who wrote in a memoir of her struggles with drug and alcohol addiction, was found in cardiac arrest at an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina, on August 16. Medics responded to the scene but were unable to resuscitate her.
Dispatch audio obtained from Broadcastify.com references a possible overdose. The coroner’s office ruled Tuesday she died of toxic effects of fentanyl and other substances, and the manner of death was ruled an accident.
Last week, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said bringing criminal cases in overdose deaths is a “big emphasis” of the DEA and prosecutors around the country.
“There’s a federal statute that allows us to go after – assuming we can prove who the dealer is – to go after them and put them in prison for murder. And we do it in every district in this country,” he said.
“So when we can prove – and sometimes if somebody is an addict, it’s difficult to prove who they actually got the pill from – but in the cases where we know who the dealer was, and we can prove beyond a reasonable doubt that the person sold the death pill to the victim who then dies, that’s a federal crime and that’s something that we will readily prosecute as often as we can.”
While the US sees tens of thousands of overdose deaths every year, criminal charges stemming from an overdose death are rare.
There were about 79,384 drug overdose deaths in the US in 2024, according to CDC data . That was a sharp decline from the previous few years, when more than 100,000 people died of drug overdoses.
By comparison, a total of 1,340 people were sentenced for a federal drug trafficking offense involving a drug overdose between fiscal years 2019 to 2023, according to a 2025 report from the US Sentencing Commission . That works out to about 270 cases per year.
About 95% of the cases involved fentanyl, a synthetic fentanyl analog or heroin, the commission’s report found. Most of the people selling or using drugs did not know the exact drugs involved, the report states.
Just over half of the defendants were street level dealers, and the average sentence in cases involving an overdose was 149 months, or over 12 years, the report found.
Building a criminal case out of a drug overdose requires two key things: Evidence of the drug’s source, and evidence the drug caused death.
For the first part, investigators use phone records, bank records, witnesses and other evidence to try to work their way up the chain to identify the dealer or supplier. But that can be difficult in the underground drug economy, as counterfeit pills may come from the streets or even strangers on the internet.
“Sometimes you’re chasing a ghost,” Honig said. “Sometimes you just can’t figure out where the end user got the drugs from, and once the chain goes cold, that’s it.”
The second challenge is proving that the specific drugs caused the death. The National Association of Attorneys General calls this the “lynchpin” of the case, saying “causation raises perhaps the most difficult issues in proving these cases.”
The challenge is that addicts may take many different substances, or they may be in bad health generally. This all means that the toxicology report and the medical examiner’s review is paramount in an overdose death, and those take time and resources.
“These damn cases are just so damn difficult to prove,” Johnson said. “You have to prove somebody sold the drugs. You have to prove that the drugs they sold caused the particular death. Those are different things.”
Though criminal overdose cases are rare, a few high-profile deaths have resulted in charges.
On October 28, 2023, Perry , the “Friends” star, was found floating face down in his hot tub at his home in Pacific Palisades, California. The Los Angeles Medical Examiner’s Office listed the cause of death as “acute effects of ketamine” and subsequent drowning.
Five people later pleaded guilty to federal drug charges resulting from his death. The defendants were identified as a woman referred to by authorities as the “Ketamine Queen,” two doctors, Perry’s live-in personal assistant and a middle-man.
The evidence against Jasveen Singh, the so-called Ketamine Queen, included text messages, phone records and the discovery of drugs in her residence during a raid, according to federal prosecutors .
‘Ketamine Queen’ sentenced in Matthew Perry case, highlighting a new era of accountability for drug dealers
Similarly, the September 2018 death of rapper Mac Miller was determined to be an accidental overdose of fentanyl, cocaine and alcohol. Prosecutors later brought charges against men who allegedly provided the rapper counterfeit oxycodone pills containing fentanyl two days before the overdose. Two men pleaded guilty and were sentenced to nearly 12 years and 17.5 years in prison, respectively, per court records.
On the other hand, there were no criminal charges filed after the April 2016 death of Prince . Authorities said there was “no reliable evidence” of who supplied the counterfeit fentanyl-laced Vicodin pills that killed him or how he obtained them.
None of the medications found in Prince’s home was prescribed to him , according to court documents. Some bottles of opioid painkillers in his home were prescribed to an associate, and other medications were found in vitamin bottles and envelopes, search warrants showed.
In Panettiere’s case, after police responded to an emergency call when she was unresponsive, her boyfriend showed an officer a bag of her medications, according to a police report.
The coroner’s office report identified her cause of death as toxic effects of fentanyl, the synthetic opioid; 4-ANPP , a chemical used to make fentanyl; Alprazolam , a benzodiazepine commonly used to treat anxiety; Methocarbamol , a muscle relaxant; and Quetiapine , an antipsychotic drug.
Ultimately, the goal of bringing these cases is to try to crack down on organized crime and deter others from illegally distributing dangerous drugs.

articles.title_orig: US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark
articles.title_zh: US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark
articles.content_orig:
The US, Denmark and Greenland have signed a defence deal that allows Washington to build two new military bases in the Arctic territory, while reaffirming Copenhagen's sovereignty over it.
Before a signing ceremony at the UN General Assembly in New York, US President Donald Trump said "we will immediately begin the process of developing a large military presence in the appropriate locations".
Danish PM Mette Frederiksen said the deal was "good for the US, Denmark and Greenland" and also for Europe and Nato, while Greenland's PM Jens-Frederik Nielsen said it was a "win-win-win".
The three leaders then inked the deal, seemingly ending more than a year of tension over the Arctic territory.
Trump had threatened to "take" the semi-autonomous Arctic territory over what he said were national security concerns, citing its strategic defence location and its mineral wealth.
His rhetoric prompted outcry from Greenlanders, Danes and European leaders who issued a joint statement saying his words "undermine transatlantic relations and risk a dangerous downward spiral".
The deal amends and updates a 1951 defence agreement between Denmark and the US.
The new pact says the US "shall be allowed to establish an additional Defence Area at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig" - referring to locations in Greenland's south and east.
Narsarsuaq is a former civilian airport and World War Two base. It has deep-water access and a large runway which US military engineers were recently surveying, the US North Command confirmed to the BBC.
The Mestersvig outpost is remote, far less developed, and used by a Danish naval dog sled unit.
The "modalities and technical details" of the bases are yet to be confirmed, and according to the deal, must be mutually agreed by all parties,
This means the US security arrangements are not unfettered and Greenland and Denmark's approval is still needed.
Washington currently operates its Pituffik Space Base in Greenland's north-west, and the new deal allows the US to "modernise and expand its activities" there.
It also says that "no state that is not a member of Nato shall be allowed to establish its own manned or unmanned military installations in Greenland nor shall they be allowed a persistent presence of military forces in Greenland".
Although the militaries of non-Nato countries are now explicitly barred from the island, it was highly unlikely that non-allied troops would have been allowed access in the first place.
Critically, no territory is ceded to the US, and it recognises both Denmark's  "sovereignty and territorial integrity" and Greenland's right to self-determination.
On one hand, that's a significant climb down from Trump's earlier calls to acquire the Arctic island.
But it does deliver a strengthened US military presence and expand on the previous agreement. Therefore to some American eyes, that will be perceived as a historic win.
The new deal must still be approved by both Denmark's and Greenland's parliaments.
Despite months of crisis, the mood at Tuesday's signing ceremony appeared strikingly upbeat and friendly.
"We going to have a tremendous relationship, a secure relationship," Trump said.
"This is tremendous for Europe and for the United States, for everybody, and for Greenland it's going to be incredible."
Meanwhile, Frederiksen described the signing of the deal as a "milestone in our long-standing co-operation".
"Seventy-five years ago we entered into an agreement about the defence of Greenland. Today, we're signing an even bigger and better agreement - a deal that can last forever."
The Danish prime minister stressed that the agreement "respects sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Kingdom of Denmark, as well as Greenland's right to self-determination".
Jens-Frederik Nielsen said that "for Greenland, it is not only an agreement about us, it is [an] agreement with us.
"It takes into account the people of Greenland, our rights, our livelihoods and the development of our country.
"Greenland matters for North American security and for transatlantic security," he said, adding that the Nato had a key role to play in the North Atlantic in a changing security situation.
The agreement also confirmed Greenland would remain in Nato if it were to gain independence from Denmark.
The 1951 agreement already allowed the US to send as many troops as it wanted to Greenland. Washington already has more than 100 military personnel permanently stationed at its Pituffik base.
Trump had tried for months to purchase or annex Greenland, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.
He argued the Arctic island was an essential piece of his plan to build a futuristic "Golden Dome" defence system to protect the US against missile attacks.
However the deal only mentions the project once, and contains no concrete proposal.
A Nato spokesperson said shortly afterwards that the military alliance welcomed the deal, which would "help advance security, stability and cooperation in this vital region".
In Denmark, the deal is being hailed as a triumph of diplomacy, and several political parties in Denmark have already said they would back it.
For Greenland, a country of 56,000 people, there was good reason for a big sigh of relief. Its leader sat side-by-side with the world's most powerful man, and got a deal that should now bring an end to months of crisis.

articles.title_orig: ‘Digger’ First Reactions Split Over Tom Cruise’s ‘Baffling,’ ‘Unpleasant’ and ‘Brave’ New Movie: ‘The Divide on This Is Going to Be Wide’
articles.title_zh: ‘Digger’ First Reactions Split Over Tom Cruise’s ‘Baffling,’ ‘Unpleasant’ and ‘Brave’ New Movie: ‘The Divide on This Is Going to Be Wide’
articles.content_orig:
Tom Cruise ‘s star vehicle “ Digger ” has finally been unveiled to members of the film press, who have been left divided by the satirical black comedy. The latest directorial effort from “Birdman” and “The Revenant” Oscar winner Alejandro González Iñárritu is being called everything from “baffling” to “unpleasant” to “fascinating stuff.” Most film journalists seem to agree on one thing: “Digger” is like nothing you’re expecting.
“This is Tom Cruise’s most dynamic and interesting role in years,” writes Next Best Picture founder Matt Neglia. “It provides him plenty of space to preach to the back row but not enough to dig deeper and deliver a performance that could’ve had far more power and nuance had Alejandro González Iñárritu’s ambitious narrative not been so imbalanced in favor of its zany but empty theatrics.” Variety’ s awards pundit Clayton Davis adds: “I respect the swing and what Alejandro González Iñárritu is going for. Tom Cruise and John Goodman are delivering stellar work, and the production design and cinematography are impressive. In the end, not all the dots connect, and I wish the film leaned harder into the absurdity and satire it kept reaching for. Shocker! The divide on this one is going to be wide.”
Awards Radar’s Joey Magidson called the movie a “mess,” claiming that “not a whole lot works here” and “this wasn’t enjoyable,” while critic Edward Douglas added: “I cannot say that ‘Digger’ is very good, although I could tell what Iñarritu and Cruise were going for… I expect a HORRENDOUS CinemaScore.” A similar opinion was shared by journalist Mike Ryan, who called the movie “unpleasant.”
IndieWire’s Jim Hemphill was more positive, writing the movie “not only showcases Tom Cruise’s best performance since ‘Magnolia,’ it’s one of the most visually inventive, conceptually audacious, and unpredictable studio movies ever made. Takes so many bold aesthetic swings it makes ‘Bardo’ look like an episode of ‘The Golden Girls.'”
Anne Thompson of IndieWire was also high on the movie, calling it “a brave and gorgeous art film that will not score with mainstream audiences but will play best for the Academy, especially crafts and actors.”
“Digger” stars Cruise as Digger Rockwell, a wealthy tycoon who must save the world when one of his oil rigs malfunctions and causes an environmental catastrophe across the planet. The film’s supporting cast includes Riz Ahmed, John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Michael Stuhlbarg and Jesse Plemons.
For Cruise, “Digger” notably marks his return to adult-oriented drama after more than a decade playing action movie heroes. In the last 10 years, Cruise’s only non-action movie is the 2017 crime comedy “American Made.” One would have to go back 20 years to add more non-action movies to Cruise’s roster, such as the musical “Rock of Ages,” the political drama “Lions for Lambs,” the comedy “Tropic Thunder” and the historical thriller “Valkyrie.” Cruise’s return to more dramatic fare has raised the eyebrows of Oscar pundits since “Digger” was announced a few years ago, but the wildly divisive reactions to “Digger” may upend his expected awards campaign.
Prior to the film’s release, much of the buzz surrounding “Digger” has related to Cruise’s wild transformation into the title role. The actor appears under heavy makeup and prosthetics that originally took six hours to apply. Cruise worked with the movie’s makeup department to get the transformation time down to an hour.
“I had a guy there with a stopwatch and I’m like, ‘OK, you see that time, six hours? By the time we’re done, we’re going to get it under an hour,’” Cruise said on the “New Heights” podcast. “They were like, ‘No, I’m not doing that, it will never happen.’ I’m like, ‘OK, first of all, if you say no, you can’t do it, you will never get there. So can we agree that we’ll maybe make it a little less?’ So with each piece that was going on, it was timed and then we’d drill and practice.”
“Digger” opens in theaters Oct. 1 from Warner Bros. Check out first reactions in the posts below.

articles.title_orig: Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol — the latest wrinkle for the Chicago Bears QB room
articles.title_zh: Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol — the latest wrinkle for the Chicago Bears QB room
articles.content_orig:
The Chicago Bears could face a quarterback conundrum on Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Backup Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent is in concussion protocol, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday, per sources. With Caleb Williams dealing with a hamstring injury that coach Ben Johnson said Monday likely puts him out this week, veteran Case Keenum could be in the starting saddle in prime time.
Bagent entered the game in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s 9-3 loss to Minnesota after Williams exited with the hamstring injury. He completed 5 of 9 passes for 54 yards. On the final play of the game, Vikings' Dallas Turner slammed Bagent to the turf for a sack.
Playing on Monday gives the Bears an extra day to get Bagent through concussion protocol before having to pull the emergency handle in Keenum.
The 38-year-old is in his second season with the Bears, mostly acting as an extra coach in the QB room. Keenum hasn’t thrown a pass or started a regular-season game since 2023 with the Houston Texans. In his 11-year career, he’s started 66 contests -- only four since 2020 -- with a career 62.3 completion percentage, 15,175 yards with 79 TDs and 51 INTs. Best known for the Minneapolis Miracle in 2017, Keenum is a wild card at this stage. Can he perform like a savvy vet who understands defenses, knows when to take his shots, and can manage the offense? Or might he look like an elderly signal-caller meant more for his film prowess than on-field acumen?
If Bagent doesn’t clear protocol by Monday night, we’ll find out.

articles.title_zh: Motorola Signature 27 Is Coming to the US to Rival Samsung’s Galaxy Phones
articles.content_orig:
Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.
Just when we thought Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro would be the last major flagship phone to be released in 2026 in the US, Motorola decided to step in by debuting the Signature 27 on Tuesday, during Qualcomm’s annual Snapdragon Summit. Unlike the original Signature , this one will be coming to US markets, and it looks like an aggressive entry into the high-end Android flagship phone market.
Motorola’s Signature 27 will include the newly announced Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 processor , coupled with a partial list of high-end features that remind me of the recently departed OnePlus phone line .
In addition to the early inclusion of Qualcomm’s chip, Motorola is touting a camera system that will include a 50-megapixel main camera along with a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto lens — the latter of which could be a boon for taking zoom photos from far distances, like at a concert. And there appear to be more cameras than Motorola has given details for, as the back of the phone shows four lenses, similar to Samsung’s quad-camera system on the Galaxy S26 Ultra .
For gamers — another audience that OnePlus had particularly focused on — the Signature 27 includes a cooling system that Motorola calls ArcticMesh. It combines a diamond-infused thermal gel, liquid metal, copper mesh and a 3D vapor chamber that’s 40% larger than the previous Signature phone — and should help it stay cool during intensive gaming and video recording.
The Signature 27 also matches Samsung’s Galaxy and Google’s Pixel lines with a seven-year commitment to software and security support, plus it will get an audio system developed in partnership with Bang & Olufsen. The Signature 27 is the first phone to get this audio system as part of a multiyear partnership with B&O, so it’s possible that down the road, the foldable Razr line will also benefit from this.
The Signature 27 will come in two colors with long names: “Pantone Coal Smoke in tactical weave” is a darker shade that features a woven texture for enhanced grip. “Pantone Capulet Olive in a brushed textile-inspired finish” is a green shade with a softer, tactile feel.
Motorola still has a lot of other details to unveil about the Signature 27, including its battery, charging speeds and display. But the first Signature phone the company debuted at CES 2026 in January included a 5,200-mAh silicon-carbon battery, 90-watt wired charging and a 6.8-inch display with a 165Hz refresh rate — all helpful reference points for what to expect in its successor. In Europe, the phone was priced at 999 euros (approximately $1,170 including tax) with 512GB of storage.
Even if the Signature 27 were to recycle some of its predecessor’s specs — and somehow hold onto its pricing despite rising costs brought on by the ongoing RAM shortage — on paper, this could be a tempting draw for former OnePlus phone fans looking for a new alternative as well as a tempting rival to Samsung’s next Galaxy phone.
We’ll find out more about the Motorola Signature 27 at a later date, with the phone set for release sometime before the end of the year.

articles.title_orig: At US-China summit, Trump should ask Xi to release my brother | Opinion
articles.title_zh: At US-China summit, Trump should ask Xi to release my brother | Opinion
articles.content_orig:
When Chinese leader Xi Jinping visits Washington this week, he is expected to bring a large delegation of Chinese business executives . The message is clear: Beijing wants America to see a China of entrepreneurship, innovation and economic opportunity that rivals the United States.
Before China made him a political prisoner, my brother Ekpar Asat embodied that promise.
In his 20s, Ekpar built Bagdax, a successful Uyghur-language multimedia technology platform in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region. A prominent Chinese tech journal named him a rising star. He believed that China’s opening to the world had created possibilities unimaginable to the generation before him.
In 2016, at the invitation of the U.S. Embassy, Ekpar traveled to the United States to participate in the State Department’s premier International Visitor Leadership Program . He met with U.S. lawmakers, exchanged ideas with American institutions and was welcomed into American homes. Ekpar returned inspired by America’s institutions, its technology sector and the families who opened their homes to him.
After Ekpar came home, Beijing detained him and said nothing. Nearly four years later, my family learned, through a Chinese Embassy response to a letter from U.S. lawmakers , that Ekpar had been sentenced to 15 years for "inciting ethnic hatred and ethnic discrimination." We have never seen a verdict, a trial record or any evidence.
The charge fails even by Beijing's own law, which caps that offense at 10 years and only in especially serious cases.
Nor does it fit the man. House Democrats noted in 2020 that Chinese media had portrayed Bagdax favorably, as a bridge across cultural divides.
The United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Ekpar's detention arbitrary. Republican and Democratic senators have said he was jailed for a " fabricated crime " and condemned his " opaque sentencing without a fair trial ." The State Department says it has raised his case with Beijing, and Congress has noted he was detained days after taking part in the department’s exchange program.
In May, the Senate passed a resolution urging President Donald Trump to prioritize the release of my brother and others in his dealings with Xi.
For a decade, the world has come to know Ekpar as a political prisoner . I knew him long before that label existed – as the best brother a sister could hope for. His colleagues knew a restless entrepreneur. Young people across the Uyghur homeland knew the platform he had built. Families knew him for helping children with disabilities and others in need. Prison did not make Ekpar significant. It interrupted a life in motion.
Ekpar began building Bagdax fresh out of college . While many of his classmates sought the security of conventional jobs, he wanted to build something new. My parents were skeptical. I wasn’t. Whenever Ekpar talked about Bagdax, he lit up. I persuaded them to let him choose his own path.
They eventually agreed, on one condition: They would provide no financial support. Ekpar started anyway. His apartment had bare cement walls, unfinished and unpainted – the first thing visitors noticed when they walked through the door. There was barely any furniture beyond a bed and a small kitchen. From that apartment, armed with his computer-science training, imagination and sheer persistence, he built Bagdax brick by brick .
That is what makes Ekpar's imprisonment more than a harrowing injustice. His story also exposes the contradiction at the heart of the economic confidence Beijing now wants to project abroad. China took a man doing precisely what governments everywhere say they want young people to do: create, innovate, build a business, serve a community, travel abroad, learn and come home.
When Xi comes to Washington, he will ask American businesses to have confidence in China. But Ekpar’s story exposes a contradiction in that pitch: What protection does business success offer when political power can still erase an entrepreneur’s freedom, business and future?
Beijing’s hypocrisy extends beyond trade. It promotes people-to-people exchange between the United States and China, yet Ekpar remains imprisoned after participating in a U.S. government exchange program.
Xi has long urged Chinese officials to tell China’s stories well , to present a China that is credible and appealing to the outside world. During his visit, President Trump should ask him about another China story: Ekpar’s. He should raise Ekpar’s case directly and ask for my brother's release.
For Xi, the test is just as straightforward. If Beijing wants Americans to believe that China is a country where entrepreneurs can build and prosper, and that Americans and Chinese can engage safely through the people-to-people exchanges both governments have long promoted, there is a simple way to demonstrate it.
Let one of those entrepreneurs, an alumnus of a U.S. government exchange program, walk free.
Rayhan Asat is a human rights lawyer and scholar. She serves as a senior legal and policy adviser and China project lead at the Atlantic Council's Strategic Litigation Project.

articles.title_orig: Soybeans, planes and rare earths: What they say about fragile U.S.-China trade truce
articles.title_zh: Soybeans, planes and rare earths: What they say about fragile U.S.-China trade truce
articles.content_orig:
Soybean purchases, orders for Boeing aircraft and access to rare earths elements — three of the headline commitments underpinning the U.S.-China trade truce — are progressing at markedly different speeds ahead of the summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping in Washington on Thursday.
Taken together, the uneven fulfillment record suggests the truce is performing its minimal function of keeping commerce moving and discouraging renewed escalation, but there is little willingness on either side to cede strategic leverage, analysts said.
"The truce is moving fastest where it costs least," Eric Xiao, head of sales for Asia at CMC Markets, told CNBC.
The superpowers' May meeting reaffirmed Beijing's commitment to increase purchases of U.S. soybeans and buy 200 Boeing aircraft , while Chinese shipments of rare earths magnets are back underway after export controls were suspended for a 12-month period beginning last November.
But delivery across the three commitments has been uneven, and difficult to verify in some cases.
Larry Hu, head of China economics at Macquarie Group, described the recent U.S.-China relationship as a phase of détente — a cooling of tensions — driven by "a balance of vulnerability."
Both sides are "acutely aware of the other's choke points," Hu said in a note.
The détente should not be mistaken for a rapprochement, according to Wendy Cutler, vice president of the Asia Society Policy Institute.
"Each side has an interest in stability right now," Cutler told CNBC's "The China Connection" in May. "This doesn't mean we're going to become best friends, but it means we're going to coexist."
Soybeans offer the clearest numerical signal of progress across the trade commitments.
China has bought almost half its 25 million ton annual commitment after it purchased roughly one million tons from U.S. producers in a single week in September, Reuters reported .
Soybean purchases are also an important tool for signaling cooperation between the two nations.
"Things pick up a little bit before the bilateral meetings between Trump and Xi ... and then fall off again," China strategist Andy Rothman told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" in July, noting that purchases tended to cluster around key meetings.
Xiao described soybean purchases as "political trophies", but cautioned against interpreting soybean fulfillment as a direct sign of Beijing's stance on broader trade ties. "China buys them because it needs them," he said.
Soybean trade tiffs are not a recent development.
China, the world's largest soybean importer, saw U.S. soybeans plummet from 40% of total imports before Trump imposed tariffs on major Chinese goods in 2018, to 23% in the first five months of 2026 .
Progress on the 200-aircraft commitment is less transparent.
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer this week said roughly 140 aircraft were in a "good state," with orders for another 10 being written, according to Reuters . Customers, models and delivery timelines have not been disclosed.
Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg has also downplayed expectations for a single 200-aircraft announcement, saying individual Chinese airlines would place and announce orders at their own pace.
The pledge came with additional caveats, with Beijing's official account of the May agreement tying the purchases to U.S. guarantees over the supply of aircraft engines and parts.
Beijing's fulfillment of the rare earths commitment is harder to measure, because the promise concerns reliable access rather than a specified export volume.
Chinese shipments of rare earths magnets to the U.S. recovered after earlier restrictions, but fell to 512 metric tons in August — down 20% from July and 13% from a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data reported by the Financial Times.
Uncertainty around rare earths access also persists for U.S. customers.
Some Chinese suppliers have declined U.S. orders because of geopolitical and compliance concerns, while some American companies have waited more than six months for export licenses, Reuters reported .
Rare earths' strategic importance may provide the clearest signal of each nation's stance on trade ties because of the strategic cost of making concessions over the materials, experts said.
Macquarie's Hu identified rare earths as the principal Chinese choke point, balanced against U.S. leverage in advanced semiconductors used in chipmaking.
Xiao similarly called rare earths the clearest indicator of the broader relationship, due to their importance in clean energy, advanced technology and defense.
Progression on the rare earths commitment could "anchor a durable relationship in a way that soybean and aircraft orders cannot," Xiao said.
He noted that exercising that leverage is a delicate calculation. A complete cutoff of exports would encourage the U.S. and its allies to accelerate alternative supply chains while hurting Chinese producers that depend on global electric vehicle and technology markets.
China's "strongest card, in other words, is one it cannot play in full," Xiao said.
– CNBC's Evelyn Cheng and Anniek Bao contributed to this story.

articles.title_orig: Trump-Xi summit puts AI safety talks on the table but neither side wants to slow down
articles.title_zh: Trump-Xi summit puts AI safety talks on the table but neither side wants to slow down
articles.content_orig:
Donald Trump wants the U.S. to beat China in the AI race. But as he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping, both countries are also weighing how to address the risks posed by rapidly advancing technology.
In recent months, AI systems have taken more consequential actions online: OpenAI said one of its research models gained unauthorized access to parts of the AI platform Hugging Face, while Anthropic found AI was being used to automate parts of cyberattacks. The incidents have raised fears that increasingly autonomous models could make attacks faster and harder to contain.
Ahead of Trump and Xi's meeting on Thursday, U.S. Treasury Scott Bessent discussed the prospect of a "U.S.-China AI dialogue" with his Chinese counterpart, He Lifeng, over the weekend, including a channel for incidents "up to a national security level."
"Leaders in both countries are spooked by the increasing cyber capabilities of AI models, and especially agents acting autonomously to escape containment and breach websites," Aalok Mehta, director of the Wadhwani AI Center at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, told CNBC.
But as fears have intensified, tensions have not dissipated.
Washington continues to restrict China's access to Nvidia's most advanced AI chips and has accused Chinese AI companies of using "distillation" — training models on the output of more advanced U.S. systems — a claim Beijing rejects.
While the U.S. took an early lead in developing large language models (LLMs), thanks to companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, Chinese models have made big capability gains in recent months and are increasingly being adopted by companies globally, including in America.
Trump previously dismissed warnings that AI poses an existential threat to humanity, risks amplified by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic chief Dario Amodei as they called for an industry slowdown and regulatory oversight.
"If we don't win AI, we're going to be put in a very bad position," Trump told reporters earlier this month.
But in a Truth Social post on Monday, he said the government "will rein things in if we have to."
The likeliest areas of agreement between the U.S. and China could be common definitions and frameworks for AI safety for powerful models and an emergency communication mechanism to discuss incidents, Mehta told CNBC.
A channel for relating national security-related incidents would be a "modest" but positive step, Chris McGuire, senior fellow for China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, told CNBC.
But an agreement to slow down AI's breakneck development speed is "extremely unlikely," he added.
China has historically used AI dialogues "to complain about U.S. export controls," McGuire said, which the U.S. uses to prevent the most advanced AI chips from being sold to China.
"Its state media has largely rejected the concerns expressed by leading U.S. AI labs about the potential for catastrophic risk, which is consistent with China's long-held skepticism of all U.S. arms control proposals," he added.
Despite U.S. restrictions, several Chinese firms have reportedly been able to access the chips' compute power remotely, via data centers in Southeast Asia.
While U.S. trade representative Jamieson Greer said controls on chips were not on the agenda during preliminary talks on the weekend, China could push to have them relaxed, said Melanie Hart, senior director of the think tank Atlantic Council's Global China Hub.
"China's asking the U.S. to embrace Chinese AI models and drop some of the U.S. controls on China's access to semiconductor chips," she told reporters on Tuesday.
Distillation could also come up in the talks. U.S. companies and officials have accused Chinese labs of using the practice to gain ground, characterizing it as theft; China rejects the allegations.
In July, Bessent threatened sanctions against companies doing it and said the Trump administration had found "watermarks of our U.S. large language models on many of the Chinese models," calling it "unacceptable."
Progress on AI cooperation relies on two things, said Mehta. "The first is that it can't hurt the ability for the U.S. and China to compete on the merits of their technology."
The second is a verification mechanism, he added. "Policymakers won't be inclined to take their counterparts just on their word, so we'll need to find ways to ensure information flowing between the two countries is accurate. That means both technical and governance verification tools."

articles.title_orig: China's Xi kicks off state visit to Washington on Wednesday with a rare planeside welcome from Trump - ABC News
articles.title_zh: China's Xi kicks off state visit to Washington on Wednesday with a rare planeside welcome from Trump - ABC News
articles.source: Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
articles.content_orig:
When Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington, he’s expected to get a rare greeting from President Donald Trump, who will be on the tarmac to welcome his counterpart’s plane instead of waiting for him to drive up to the White House
WASHINGTON -- When Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington on Wednesday, he's expected to get a rare greeting from President Donald Trump , who will be on the tarmac to welcome his counterpart's plane instead of waiting for him to drive up to the White House.
Trump's decision to greet Xi at Joint Base Andrews just outside Washington rather than receiving him at the executive residence shows how far the U.S. president is going to honor China's leader as he makes his first state visit in more than a decade.
The White House has not released many details about Wednesday's greeting, but Trump is expected to participate in an arrival ceremony at the base with Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan. The salutation will kick off a three-day visit that's expected to be saturated with pomp, even by White House standards. The state visit, complete with a formal state dinner at the White House on Thursday, is supposed to reciprocate for the ceremonial grandeur that marked Trump's May visit to China.
But it's also a showy patina at a time when tensions between the two geopolitical rivals are high over trade, artificial intelligence, Trump's war with Iran and China's designs on Taiwan.
Beyond using the visit to try to keep “strategic stability” between the two countries, Trump seems to be pulling out all the diplomatic stops to show off for Xi. He has lavished praise on him as a “great leader” and described a warm relationship with the man he has called a friend. That's all while he's given Xi a pass on many issues .
Mississippi Sen. Roger Wicker, the Republican chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, criticized the “lavish welcome." He said during a speech on the Senate floor on Tuesday that Trump should not have invited the Chinese leader “based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party.”
Wicker archly suggested a list of topics that Trump could discuss with Xi at the state dinner, such as “the purposes of China’s massive military buildup, or about China’s clear support for Iran,” saying that “during every minute of dialogue” Trump should keep in mind that “his guest is a brutal, unelected and oppressive dictator who seeks to dominate his neighbors and whose massive military arsenal is aimed directly at the United States of America.”
Trump has made it clear he wants to wow Xi , telling reporters in recent weeks that he was delighted his new “work of art” helicopter landing pad would be ready for the visit while bemoaning that his massive White House ballroom would not.
On Wednesday, Trump is expected to try to match the pageantry he was met with in China earlier this year. Xi wasn't there to meet Trump — he sent Chinese Vice President Han Zheng instead. But there was a long red carpet rolled out to meet Air Force One in Beijing. Along the sides were a military honor guard, a military band and about 300 Chinese youths waving Chinese and American flags and chanting, “Welcome, welcome! Warm welcome!” The children were wearing white and light blue uniforms that mirrored the traditional paint colors of the presidential plane.
Trump's airport ceremony will be followed on Thursday by more formalities, including an arrival ceremony at the White House and a review of troops. Before the black-tie dinner — which will feature tech industry leaders like Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and SpaceX’s Elon Musk — the two leaders are expected to dive into the weighty issues behind closed doors, even as expectations are low that the trip will produce any major breakthroughs in the relationship.
On Friday, Xi and Peng will be back at the White House for a private tea with the president and first lady Melania Trump before joining them on a tour of the National Archives in Washington. The White House has said they will view historic documents underscoring the relationship between the two countries.
Associated Press writer Mary Clare Jalonick contributed to this report.

阿里巴巴宣布这一消息之际，包括Anthropic首席执行官Dario Amodei在内的美国人工智能领导者警告称，中国的人工智能发展对美国构成威胁，并呼吁全面放缓该技术的发展。中国领导人Xi将于周三抵达华盛顿，进行国事访问，并与美国总统唐纳德·特朗普举行会晤，预计届时将讨论人工智能、贸易和关税问题。

阿里巴巴还表示，计划以5到10万亿个参数的规模训练一个新的人工智能模型，这是衡量人工智能学习能力的一个指标，使其更接近美国最先进的模型。其最新的Qwen3.8-Max模型是其Qwen AI系列模型中最强大的，有2.4万亿个参数。中国人工智能公司Moonshot表示，其7月份发布的Kimi K3是世界上最大的开放模型，拥有2.8万亿个参数。
阿里巴巴还强调了扩大为其云计算业务提供动力的数据中心的计划，理由是对人工智能计算的需求呈“指数级”增长。该公司表示，预计到2032年，其计算能力将超过20吉瓦。截至今年年中，SpaceX拥有约1.4吉瓦的人工智能计算能力，并表示其目标是在2027年达到10吉瓦以上。

articles.title_orig: Ahead of US, China meeting, Trump and Xi both face crossroads | Opinion
articles.title_zh: Ahead of US, China meeting, Trump and Xi both face crossroads | Opinion
articles.content_orig:
Ahead of US, China meeting, Trump and Xi both face crossroads | Opinion
The Chinese leader has to deal with a legitimacy crisis at home. The U.S. leader knows that Republicans' success in the midterm elections depend on economic relief for the American people, fast.
A leadership summit between any two countries is always cause for pressure-packed preparations by all relevant agencies, but for the Sept. 24 White House U.S.-China summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the stakes have arguably never been higher.
China faces the loss of 18 million factory jobs, rampant income inequality and a 70% increase in rural protests between 2024 and 2025.
The United States faces skyrocketing oil prices, persistent threats of escalation from Iran and China’s alarming trade surplus.
For big "bilaterals" like this one set for Thursday, every Cabinet agency and all senior White House staff scurry to put together an agenda. Here are strategies they'll likely submit to the president as bases for memorandums of understanding, which will come from the meetings if executed well.
Trump, Xi should call for a world conference on AI
Trump and Xi, first and foremost, could agree to participate in and lead a world conference on artificial intelligence, with positive usages and safeguards.
Trump must seek a halt to China’s rampant intellectual property theft, which has enabled Chinese companies to save billions of dollars training their AI on American frontier models.
However, because both countries deeply mistrust the other to fairly navigate AI safety on their own, the leaders must address patent and copyright theft laws, and implement AI guardrails against human harm. Offered in a spirit of friendly competitors, this could benefit both countries and the world.
A joint statement could be significant.
Gain more rare earth metals for the United States
In 2025, Beijing began requiring foreign companies to obtain a special government-approved license to ship certain products containing rare earth metals sourced from China.
To obtain these licenses, companies had to share highly sensitive data, including profiles of end-users.
Companies affiliated with foreign militaries would be largely denied licenses unless Washington maintains some information access (now recognizing U.S. military’s dependence on Chinese rare earth elements) but the United States and China could agree on mutual assistance.
There could be higher tariffs or tighter restrictions on China’s access to semiconductors unless China withdraws its expanded license requirements.
Clarify US-China research collaboration
Recently, millions of dollars of Washington funding for colleges has helped Beijing develop critical military technology through academic research involving organizations affiliated with China’s defense industrial base, according to a House Republican report.
In response, clarify and regulate more strongly research collaboration between American universities and Chinese-military-affiliated organizations.
Negotiate guardrails on tech components that can spy
Mounting evidence reveals that Chinese tech components can secretly transmit information to China.
This is a massive national security risk, particularly due to the U.S. military’s reliance on Chinese batteries. Trump must secure restrictions on components sold to the United States with surveillance capabilities.
Maintain strategic ambiguity on Taiwan
Taiwan remains the strictest red line for China, so any diplomatic negotiation requires strategic ambiguity on Taiwan contingencies. Remain vague about whether the United States would militarily support Taiwan in the case of a Chinese invasion.
Keep the $14 billion pending Taiwan arms sale up for negotiation and leave for later after this summit, depending on Xi’s openness to other demands, and signal support for China while keeping future options open to support Taiwan if necessary.
Pledge to reduce oil prices
Washington wants Beijing to buy American goods. Unfortunately, rising oil prices from the Iran war exacerbated production costs in China, slowing down its economic growth, and driving the Chinese to buy fewer American goods.
Trump could pledge de-escalation attempts with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to bring down oil prices. Clarify that China should stop buying Iranian oil until the Strait of Hormuz is opened, and that China should expand its agreement to import more American agricultural goods.
Cooperate on drug policy, target methamphetamine and fentanyl
Expand the McCaffrey-China anti-drug agreement made more than a quarter-century ago on methamphetamine and now fentanyl.
In 2000, retired Army Gen. Barry McCaffrey, as head of the Office of National Drug Control Policy, led a delegation to China and negotiated a drug treatment and source prevention agreement. He explained that for China itself, treatment was more than warehousing thousands of addicts cold turkey in a big room in a Chinese city. It meant stop allowing import of drugs from Myanmar, formerly known as Burma, and providing jobs and counseling for addicts.
Now, China is a major source of devastating fentanyl in the United States. An agreement to help each other could be a productive component of the Trump-Xi summit.
To solidify long-term trust, Trump should increase cultural ties between the two nations by renewing a commitment to sharing arts and sports – like Chinese table tennis and U.S. football diplomacy – and inviting China’s National Peking Opera back to the United States.
Both Trump and Xi are at a crossroads
Xi faces a legitimacy crisis. While many of his citizens have long supported the Chinese Communist Party’s overall economic prosperity, China’s stagnating economy and skyrocketing youth unemployment have greatly weakened the party's internal political legitimacy.
For his part, Trump’s reversing his low approval ratings ahead of the November midterm elections (and, consequently, the Republican Party’s success) depends on his ability to deliver economic relief, and fast. That can be accomplished by increasing American exports to China.
Chinese leaders are as interested in making productive deals with the United States as we are with them, making the Trump-Xi summit an enormous opportunity for the two global superpowers as well as the world.
Robert Weiner was a spokesman in the Clinton and George W. Bush administrations, the White House drug policy spokesman, chief of staff for the House Aging Committee, and communications director of the House Government Operations and Oversight Committee. Emmbrooke Flather is a senior policy analyst at Robert Weiner Associates, and served as copresident of the Chinese Culture Club at Phillips Academy Andover. At Boston College, she studied Mandarin, East Asian Security and the Rise of China.

articles.title_orig: Egypt, China unearth wine press at temple to ancient goddess
articles.title_zh: Egypt, China unearth wine press at temple to ancient goddess
articles.content_orig:
A limestone structure believed to have once served as a wine press was recently unearthed at the Temple of Sekhmet site near the village of Mit Rahina, the Egyptian Tourism and Antiquities Ministry announced earlier this month.
Mit Rahina is located near the ancient ruins of Memphis, which in antiquity had served as the capital of the first nome of Lower Egypt.
In ancient Egyptian mythology, Sekhemet is considered both a warrior goddess and a goddess of medicine. Her temple makes up one part of the Great Temple of Ptah complex, which served as the main temple of ancient Memphis.
Discovered by a joint Egyptian-Chinese archaeological mission, the wine press includes an upper basin sloping downward toward a central opening and a lower collection basin, each topped with an opening designed to hold amphorae.
Archaeologists found grape seeds inside the press, supporting the archaeologists’ interpretation.
Dr. Hisham El-Leithy, Secretary-General of the Supreme Council of Antiquities, explained that the mission began its work by cleaning and documenting the Temple of Sekhmet as part of its excavations to understand how the site was used throughout the ages.
Mudbrick residential complex also unearthed
Additionally, the mission found the remains of a mudbrick residential complex in the area surrounding the temple, along with a series of stone blocks and statue fragments believed to have been part of Ptah’s temple.
Most of the blocks and fragments date back to the New Kingdom period, mainly during the reign of King Ramesses II, and are made from various types of stone, including limestone, red granite, and schist
Other artifacts found at the site include pottery shards, faience amulets, small terracotta and limestone statuettes, ostraca, and votive stelae.
Mohamed Abdel-Badie, head of the Egyptian Antiquities Sector at the Supreme Council of Antiquities, explained that these discoveries indicate that there had been continuous human settlement in the area between the Third Intermediate Period and the Late Period, through the Ptolemaic era and up to the Greco-Roman period.
Egypt’s Tourism and Antiquities Minister Sherif Fathy expressed his pleasure at the collaboration between Egypt and China, two of the oldest civilizations in history.
The Temple of Sekhmet was discovered by chance in 1959, during the construction of a house in the area. Following this, Egyptian antiquities inspector Mohamed Abdel Tawab El-Hetta carried out a single season of excavations at the site from 1961 to 1962.
In 2015, the visible remains of the temple were documented as part of the Ancient Memphis Site and Community Management Project.
Deity-inscribed tombstones, sarcophagi unearthed at ancient Egyptian burial site
Earlier this summer, some 20 limestone tombstones, several sarcophagi, and a collection of funerary amulets were discovered during excavations at the Tell El Deir archaeological site.
The sides and backs of the tombstones are decorated with religious symbols and godly imagery, including that of a griffin, Agathodaemon, and Isis-Thermouthis.
Agathodaemon is a lesser serpent demon in ancient Graeco-Egyptian religion, as well as in classical Greek mythology. Isis-Thermouthis is a combination of the Egyptian goddess Isis, the sister and wife of Osiris, and Renenutet (Thermuthis), the Egyptian goddess of grain.
The appearance of the two deities on the tombstones points to joint Greek and Roman influence on ancient Egyptian heritage and funerary practices.
Further, the decorations allow archaeologists to identify the social status of the tombstones’ owners.
Additionally, the Egyptian archaeological mission operating at the site uncovered a collection of pottery incense burners, decorated lamps, and funerary amulets, as well as several barrel-shaped anthropoid ceramic coffins.

Why Brunei prefers ‘quiet diplomacy’ over confrontation in South China Sea
As a nation with a small military, Brunei would rather work with Beijing in safe zones such as peacekeeping than butt heads, analysts say
Brunei’s measured defence ties with Beijing reflect its low-key approach to South China Sea disputes, with analysts saying that goals such as peacekeeping offer the safest room for both sides to maintain diplomacy.
A meeting between Bruneian and Chinese defence officials in Beijing last week, when both nations pledged closer practical cooperation and support for regional stability, underscored that tact.
But observers also expect ties to remain modest, constrained by maritime claims and Bandar Seri Begawan’s preference for a diversified network of security partners.
Last Tuesday, Brunei Defence Minister Halbi Mohammad Yussof led a delegation to meet Chinese counterpart Admiral Dong Jun on the sidelines of the 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum.

articles.content_orig:
How does Xi Jinping’s ‘special plane’ compare with Air Force One?
A look at the Chinese leader’s aircraft, which is bound to become part of the visual choreography of his state visit in Washington
The aircraft carrying China’s leader, often referred to in state media and official statements as a zhuan ji, or special plane, remains far less known to the world than Air Force One, despite both countries using Boeing 747s for presidential travel.
For a head of state, a presidential aircraft is more than a means of transport. Its range, on-board facilities and security systems reflect the practical demands of presidential travel and diplomatic missions, and the aircraft itself becomes part of the visual choreography of a state visit.
In one sense, it is one of the first symbols of a country to arrive in the host country, appearing in the sky before the president steps onto the tarmac.
articles.content_zh:

对于国家元首来说，总统专机不仅仅是一种交通工具。它的航程、机载设施和安全系统反映了总统旅行和外交使团的实际需求，飞机本身也成为国事访问视觉编排的一部分。从某种意义上说，它是一个国家抵达东道国的首批象征之一，在总统走上停机坪之前出现在天空中。

articles.title_orig: Taiwan is watching closely as Xi and Trump meet and hopes US will keep up its arms sales
articles.title_zh: Taiwan is watching closely as Xi and Trump meet and hopes US will keep up its arms sales
articles.content_orig:
TAINAN, Taiwan (AP) — As China’s Xi Jinping arrives in Washington to meet with U.S. President Donald Trump, Taiwan expressed confidence that U.S. arms sales to the island that Beijing claims as its own will continue — despite China’s pressure.
China has pressed Washington to halt the arms sales, most prominently during a summit in May between Trump and Xi in Beijing. After that meeting, the United States paused the sale of a record-breaking $14 billion package — and Trump described arms sales to Taiwan as a “very good negotiating chip” with China.
Still, the U.S. government and Congress have “repeatedly expressed support for Taiwan’s self-defense capabilities,” Taiwanese Defense Ministry spokesperson Maj. Gen. Chiao Fu-chun told reporters in the southern city of Tainan.
“We will continue to maintain close contact with the U.S. Department of War and continue to push forward the arms procurement deal between Taiwan and the U.S., ensuring it proceeds as planned,” he added.
The U.S. is bound by its own laws to provide Taiwan — a self-ruled democracy that China sees as its own territory — with the means to defend itself. While not recognizing Taiwan as a country, the U.S. is the island’s strongest informal backer and arms provider.
Washington approved another $11 billion package for Taiwan in December.
Hours before Xi’s arrival for the three-day state visit to the U.S., Taiwan’s military on Wednesday conducted live fire drills featuring a domestically developed eight-wheeled armored vehicle, highlighting efforts to strengthen its own arms production.
Called The Cheetah, the vehicle can be fitted with a 105-millimeter (4.1-inch) cannon and can reach a maximum speed of about 100 kph (62 mph) and an operational range of about 500 kilometers (311 miles).
Taiwanese Maj. Gen. Chen Chien-chung said the vehicle can be used on various terrains and is suitable for urban warfare.
Trump has in recent years pressed Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te to dramatically increase Taiwan’s defense budget. The budget will exceed 3% of Taiwan’s gross domestic product for the first time in 2027, and Lai has pledged to get to 5% by 2030.
Mistreanu reported from Taipei, Taiwan.

articles.title_orig: Trump administration accuses banned media outlets of 'falsehoods' ahead of court hearing
articles.title_zh: Trump administration accuses banned media outlets of 'falsehoods' ahead of court hearing
articles.content_orig:
Trump administration accuses banned media outlets of 'falsehoods' ahead of court hearing
The US Justice Department has filed documents that accuse three media outlets banned from the White House of "trafficking in verifiable falsehoods" and reporting which "threatened national security" as it prepared to defend the move in court.
Last week, President Donald Trump barred CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news".
After their reporters had their passes confiscated and were denied access to the building, the three outlets jointly launched legal action, calling the move unconstitutional.
On Wednesday, a judge is set to decide whether to issue an order temporarily lifting the ban, pending a full hearing.
According to a court filing by the Justice Department in a District of Columbia court, the three outlets were issued with a list of "reporting incidents" by the White House ahead of the ban.
The filing cites a number of stories about construction at the White House - including about a security bunker and the building of a new ballroom, as well as a report on an internal information leak investigation.
It goes on to say that "access to the White House is a privilege, not a right".
The three media organisations have argued that the ban breaches their rights under the First Amendment, which forbids the government from "abridging" the freedom of the press.
In a joint statement confirming legal action against the government, they said: "Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting.
"Left unchallenged, this threatens press freedom and the public's right to independent journalism free from government interference."
Major TV networks have withdrawn from a media-sharing arrangement of video and images of the president, known as the pool, in protest over the ban.
Shortly after, the White House launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, which operates a 24/7 feed of clips of the president.

The investigation into the 36-year-old US actress’ death is ongoing, police say
US actress Hayden Panettiere died from an accidental overdose of several drugs, including fentanyl, a coroner in South Carolina said on Tuesday.
Panettiere, 36, was found unresponsive in an apartment in Greenville, South Carolina, on August 16. Her on-and-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson and his brother Zach Hickerson were at the home.
According to a statement from the Greenville County Coroner’s Office, a combination of fentanyl and its chemical by-product, as well as the anti-anxiety medication alprazolam, a muscle relaxant and a drug used to treat major depression and other serious mental health disorders, was found in Panettiere’s system.
The office did not include further details from the autopsy report in its initial release.
